method: Original retire loop, endpoint-ring removal, link state reset, contact clearing and pointer-vector reserve run natively; only the two protected pool-return blocks (0x19587e9, 0x1958bd1) and the allocator vtable entries (+8/+0x10/+0x18) are supplied. Python side composes retire with the existing ring-removal, link-reset and reserve reconstructions.
comparisons: ordered pool-return and allocator calls with every argument
0x90-byte link snapshot at each pool-return call
all fixture bytes: provider, queue owners, initial and newly allocated queue arrays, bodies, links, contact arrays, output descriptor and array
divide-fault occurrence and partial state for divisor 0
coverage: 0..24 links attached to selector1 rings over four bodies; random subset selected in random order
queue owners with null/nonnull storage, capacities 0..8, full and nonfull counts
mutation trials redirecting the provider slot and filling an owner vector during reset
direct reserve leaf: no-op, allocate, reallocate, release, count clamp and 32-bit size truncation
failure_proof: Reading the provider slot after reset instead of before fails at retire case 81 (owner bytes differ).
Clamping count only above capacity+1 fails at reserve leaf case 46.
limits: Ring fixtures are built by the reconstructed attach (itself natively validated), not by native attach in this harness.
Protected pool-return blocks, locks and allocator internals are supplied stand-ins; the authored allocator mirror is not engine behavior.
Consumers of the provider+0x70 queue vectors are not reconstructed.
Divisor-0 divide fault is compared only as fault occurrence plus memory state.
No live validation or concurrent mutation guarantee.
